MENTOR: So Dot 1 goes first, then Dot 2, then Dot 3, each starting 4 frames after the one before.

Right now all three Dots start moving at 0.5 s, so at 1 s they've all been moving for the same half second. I rendered that frame, but it came back too small for me to make out the dots, so scrub to 1 s in your own viewer. When everything starts on the same frame, nothing leads the eye, and the three read as one block instead of a sequence.

Your turn. Stagger them so Dot 1 starts first, Dot 2 starts 4 frames after it, and Dot 3 starts 4 frames after Dot 2. You can do it any of these ways:

- **Drag the keys:** select all the keys on a layer by dragging a box around them in the timeline, then drag them later.
- **Drag the layer's bar:** grab the middle of a Dot's bar and drag it later. The bar's keys move with it. Don't drag an end of the bar, because that trims it and leaves the keys where they were.
- **Quick Offset:** select the layers, hold Command and Option, and drag. After Effects spreads them out evenly as you drag.

Play it back, and say "done" when you're happy with it.
